description: Phase 3: Ingest/Export + MCP Server. Full agent workflow: upload a project, run commands, download results. MCP tools work in MCP Inspector. 9 stories across 2 epics.

userStories.title: POST /v1/sandboxes/:id/ingest — tar.gz upload
userStories.description: As an API consumer, I want to upload a tar.gz archive and extract it into the sandbox.
acceptanceCriteria: Writes archive to sandbox FS at `/tmp/_ingest.tar.gz`
Runs `mkdir -p $basePath && cd $basePath && tar xzf /tmp/_ingest.tar.gz && rm /tmp/_ingest.tar.gz` via bash.exec
Route is mounted on the main Hono app in server.ts
Unit test: ingest tar.gz of 3 files, verify files readable in sandbox
userStories.notes: Uses sessionManager.withSession to get bash and fs instances. Hono has multipart/form-data support via c.req.parseBody(). Existing routes are in src/api/routes/.

userStories.title: POST /v1/sandboxes/:id/ingest-files — JSON manifest upload
userStories.description: As an API consumer, I want to upload files via JSON for small/programmatic uploads.
acceptanceCriteria: Body validated by zod: { basePath: string, files: Record<string, string> } where values are base64-encoded content
Decodes each file from base64, writes to basePath + '/' + relativePath via fs.writeFile
Creates parent directories as needed (mkdir -p behavior)
Unit test: ingest 3 files via JSON, verify content matches after base64 decode
Unit test: missing basePath or files returns 400 validation error
userStories.notes: Uses sessionManager.withSession. Reuse validateBody from src/api/validation.ts for zod validation.

userStories.title: GET /v1/sandboxes/:id/export — tar.gz download
userStories.description: As an API consumer, I want to download sandbox contents as a tar.gz archive.
acceptanceCriteria: Runs `tar czf /tmp/_export.tar.gz -C $basePath .` via bash.exec inside the sandbox
Reads archive bytes from sandbox FS via fs.readFileBuffer('/tmp/_export.tar.gz')
Returns Content-Type: application/gzip with Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=export.tar.gz
Returns 404 if basePath does not exist
Unit test: write files to sandbox, export, verify response is gzip with correct headers
userStories.notes: Uses sessionManager.withSession to get bash and fs instances. bash.exec runs tar inside the virtual FS.

userStories.title: MCP server setup and streamable HTTP transport
userStories.description: As a developer, I want an MCP server using streamable HTTP transport mounted on the Hono app.
acceptanceCriteria: Server info includes name ('virtualfs') and version (from package.json or hardcoded)
MCP endpoint mounted on Hono app at /mcp path in server.ts
Handles POST /mcp for client requests and GET /mcp for SSE stream
Install @modelcontextprotocol/sdk as dependency if not already present
Unit test: MCP server initializes without error
userStories.notes: The MCP SDK provides Server class and StreamableHTTPServerTransport. Mount as Hono route that bridges to the MCP transport. Check @modelcontextprotocol/sdk docs for the latest transport API.

userStories.title: MCP tool — sandbox_create
userStories.description: As an AI agent, I want to create a sandbox via MCP.
acceptanceCriteria: Tool description: 'Create an isolated bash sandbox with a virtual filesystem' (under 80 chars)
Input schema: { env?: Record<string, string> } (optional environment variables)
Tool registered on MCP server in src/api/mcp/server.ts
Unit test: calling sandbox_create tool returns a sandbox id
userStories.notes: MCP tools use server.tool(name, schema, handler) pattern from the SDK. The handler receives parsed args.

userStories.title: MCP tool — sandbox_delete
userStories.description: As an AI agent, I want to delete a sandbox via MCP.
acceptanceCriteria: Tool description: 'Delete a sandbox and all its files'
Input schema: { id: string } (required sandbox ID)
Returns error content if sandbox not found
Unit test: create then delete sandbox via MCP tools

userStories.title: MCP tool — bash_exec
userStories.description: As an AI agent, I want to execute bash in a sandbox via MCP. This is the primary tool for all file and directory operations.
acceptanceCriteria: Tool description is multi-line and lists supported commands (cat, echo, ls, find, mkdir, rm, mv, cp, touch, chmod, stat, grep, sed, awk, sort, pipes, redirects, etc.) and NOT supported commands (curl, wget, apt, npm, vi, background jobs, process control, /proc, /sys, symlinks, compilers, interpreters)
Input schema: { id: string, script: string, timeout?: number }
Handler uses sessionManager.withSession(id, async (session) => session.bash.exec(script, { timeout }))
Returns JSON content: { stdout: string, stderr: string, exitCode: number }
Buffered execution (not streaming) — full result in one response
Unit test: execute 'echo hello' via bash_exec returns { stdout: 'hello\n', exitCode: 0 }
userStories.notes: The detailed tool description helps AI agents understand what just-bash supports and does not support. This avoids agents trying to use curl, pip, etc.

userStories.title: MCP tool — fs_ingest
userStories.description: As an AI agent, I want to upload multiple files into a sandbox in one call.
acceptanceCriteria: Tool description: 'Upload files into sandbox (use before bash_exec to seed project files)'
Input schema: { id: string, basePath?: string, files: Record<string, string> }
basePath defaults to '/home/user'; relative paths in files are joined to basePath
Content is plain text (not base64) — simpler for agents
Creates all parent directories automatically via fs.mkdir with recursive option
Returns JSON content: { ok: true, count: number }
Unit test: ingest 3 files, verify readable via bash_exec 'cat'
userStories.notes: Unlike the HTTP ingest-files endpoint (US-072) which uses base64, MCP fs_ingest uses plain text for simpler agent interaction.

userStories.title: MCP tool — fs_export
userStories.description: As an AI agent, I want to download all files from a sandbox path as a JSON map.
acceptanceCriteria: Tool description: 'Download files from sandbox as JSON map'
Input schema: { id: string, path?: string }
Walks the directory tree recursively, reads each file
Returns JSON content: { files: Record<string, string> } with file paths relative to the given path
UTF-8 text files returned as plain text; binary files returned as base64 with a marker
Skips directories in the output (only files)
Unit test: write files to sandbox, export via fs_export, verify map contains correct content
userStories.notes: Uses fs.getAllPaths() or fs.readdir recursive to enumerate files, then fs.readFile for each. Binary detection: try UTF-8 decode, check for replacement chars.
